question: Should OpenClaw adopt the public `registerReadinessCriterion` Plugin SDK contract and its operator-selectable readiness model before accepting four built-in hosting profiles built on top of it?
rationale: This is a durable external plugin API and a new readiness-admission product contract; code review cannot determine whether maintainers want that compatibility commitment or the proposed built-in profile scope.

options.title: Approve the readiness platform first
options.body: Confirm the public readiness SDK and land the prerequisite readiness work before reviewing this profile layer as a narrower follow-on.

options.title: Keep readiness core-only
options.body: Reject or defer plugin criteria, then ask for a reduced hosting-profile proposal that uses only accepted core-owned observations.

options.title: Defer profiles entirely
options.body: Keep current readiness behavior while maintainers decide whether named deployment postures belong in core at all.

recommendation.title: Approve the readiness platform first
recommendation.body: Confirm the public readiness SDK and land the prerequisite readiness work before reviewing this profile layer as a narrower follow-on.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed participant carrying all three linked readiness-stack branches, though the final direction requires a Gateway/plugin-SDK owner decision.
